title: Victoria Spivey, the studio house band and record executives
summary: Russell's men served as house band in the studio, recording with anyone, including Spivey, Wilton Crawley and Bob Hope, with Russell handling the business.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: My first record date: sessions, personnel, discography

blocks.x: Charlie Holmes (1/14/83):
...not too well. But I mean, you know, just from in the studio. That's the only place I ever seen him. But I don't remember a sister. Sweet T(?). I don't remember that.
Well, how did you get together with Victoria?
I didn't get together with her. She was at the studio, just like... It was Russell's group, you know...
I see.

And when we'd go the studio we'd never know who was going to show up there. We were like what you would call the house band, one of them things. We would record with anybody that they had, you know. They would call Russell up, Russell would send so many of us to the gig, to the studio. Sometimes it would be Victoria. Sometimes it would be Wilton Crawley or somebody else. Anybody. We was recording with everybody.

Sometimes we made a thing with Bob Hope. Yeah, Bob Hope. I will never forget his theme song, you know, and we were playing his theme song. I mean, we were just like on the staff, you know, at that studio.
Who was the man at the studio who would call Russell? Do you remember that?
Oh, let me see. There were so many of... There wasn't so many, I mean... It's according to what
Holmes (1/14) - 2

studio. See, I never got involved with the higher-ups, you know what I mean, because they were... As far as Russell was concerned... He did all the business where I was concerned. I know one of them was named Jack Something... Jack Kapp. Jack Kapp. I think he was from Okeh Records. I think, I'm not sure it was Jack Kapp. Then there was another fellow... Boy, I can't remember his name now.
See, I had no business with them. You know what I mean...
Right, because they all went through Russell.
Yeah. And consequently... I mean, I knew their names at the time. But I don't remember them now.
Now, Victoria's sister's name was Addie -- Addie Spivey.
Addie Stephens?
Addie Spivey.
Oh, Spih-vee [PHONETIC]
Addie Spivey. You don't remember her.
No. I guess she was there because I heard a record, and that's me on the record with her. But I don't remember her.
Okay.
I mean, we made records and things that I didn't know who the people were. You know what I mean?
Holmes (1/14) - 3
Unless they had a big name or something. No, I don't remember her sister.
